title: indigo_ccd_atik: Atik Infinity no longer connects since the generator migration (3.0-8+)
description:
User report: an Atik Infinity Color connects and works with INDIGO 3.0-1 but fails to connect with 3.0-9 and 3.0-11 (two clean upgrades from the 3.0-1 indigosky armhf image; Raspberry Pi 3 Model B, Raspbian 12 bookworm 32-bit, kernel 6.12.93+rpt-rpi-v7, usbfs buffer 192MiB). In the web UI and ain-imager the connection fails; in Ekos the user reports a crash on connect. Other devices on the same server (Player One Ceres 462M, SynScan mount, Moonlite focuser) keep working.

Analysis so far (code reading only, not reproduced): the driver was migrated to the code generator on 2026-09-12 (released in 3.0-8); the bundled armhf libatikcameras.so (2025.06.30.2074) is unchanged since November 2025, so the difference is in driver code. The hand-written driver ignored the results of ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo, ArtemisCoolingInfo and ArtemisGetMaxBin (comment 'Temporary workaround for SDK_2020_06_23') and only set ALERT on the window heater and preset properties when their readout failed. atik_initialize_ccd() in indigo_ccd_atik.driver now fails the whole connection when: ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo or ArtemisCoolingInfo returns anything other than ARTEMIS_OK or ARTEMIS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED; the camera reports cooling flags (flags & 3) == 3 with max <= min or without a temperature sensor; ArtemisGetMaxBin fails or returns out-of-range values; the window heater or preset/gain/offset readout fails. The migrated driver was hardware-tested with Atik Titan, Atik One and Atik 11000 only, not with an Infinity. Less likely alternative: atik_open() now locates the camera by serial number instead of by index and fails there.

The Ekos crash is not explained by the failed connection path (the generated handler calls atik_close only after a successful atik_open) and may be a separate defect.

A debug log (indigo_server -vv, including the SDK debug callback output) of a connection attempt on 3.0-11 and of the Ekos crash has been requested from the reporter. Wait for it, or reproduce with the fake SDK, before fixing, so the fix targets the call that actually fails.

Proposed fix: a failure of an optional capability query (temperature sensor, cooling, window heater, presets/gain/offset) hides that capability instead of refusing the connection; keep a hard failure only for ArtemisProperties, sensor geometry and buffer allocation. Add fake SDK tests for an uncooled camera whose capability queries return error codes, and bump the driver version.

Required: the comment above uncooled_camera_with_failing_capability_queries (test_ccd_atik_sdk.c:1000-1005) presents the hypothesis as the reproduced cause and calls the Infinity uncooled; reword as a model of an unconfirmed hypothesis. Non-blocking: (1) the paths that still refuse the connection (atik_open serial lookup / ArtemisConnect NULL, ArtemisProperties failure or invalid geometry/pixel size) log nothing, so a reporter log would not decide between the remaining candidates; (2) .driver:128-131 comment should cite the old SDK_2020_06_23 workaround; (3) cooler log does not say the reason is the missing temperature sensor; (4) temperature hidden silently when TemperatureSensorInfo(1) returns NOT_IMPLEMENTED after sensors > 0; (5) branch TemperatureSensorInfo(0) OK and (1) failing not exercised separately; (6) the no-poll assertion of the uncooled case is weak. The --no-build record is valid (the test compiles the driver source itself).

Round 2 (same independent reviewer, claude-opus-5-5 high), head 7aa87c9ec: pass. The hardware record made at e3d55ba66 stays valid: the delta is logging on refusal/hidden paths only. Non-blocking: a connect to an unplugged, not yet detached camera logs 'No camera with serial' at ERROR; both records carry 3.0.0.51 while logging changed between them.

Implementation note (fake SDK reproduction, no hardware touched).

CAUSE (hypothesis, reproduced with the fake SDK only, NOT confirmed on an Atik Infinity): atik_initialize_ccd() of the generated driver (3.0.0.50) refuses the whole connection when an optional capability query fails or answers out of range. The pre-migration driver (4ff475376, ccd_connect_callback) ignored those results. A fake camera that is uncooled and answers ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo, ArtemisCoolingInfo, ArtemisGetMaxBin, ArtemisGetWindowHeaterPower and ArtemisCameraSpecificOptionGetData with ARTEMIS_INVALID_FUNCTION fails to connect on 3.0.0.50 (CONNECTION ALERT) and connects on 3.0.0.51. The coordinator's hardware check (Atik VS, Raspberry Pi arm64, 3.0.0.50) connects fine; the VS has temperature control, so these failure branches were not exercised there. Which query the Infinity actually fails, if any, is unknown until a -vv log arrives; 3.0.0.51 logs every hidden capability with the SDK result code at INFO level (indigo_server -v).

STEP 1 - places where 3.0.0.50 refuses what the pre-migration driver accepted (connect path, call by call):
1. Discovery/open: old plug attached every SDK index even when ArtemisDeviceSerial failed (serial "") and never called ArtemisDeviceIsCamera; old connect used ArtemisConnect(index) directly. New plug skips devices that are not cameras, have no NUL-terminated non-empty serial or no name; atik_open rescans ArtemisDeviceSerial and connects only on a serial match. Not changed: plug and open use the same lookup, the reporter's camera appeared, and the VS run proves the serial lookup works ("65535 65535").
2. ArtemisProperties: both refuse a failed call. New also refuses nPixelsX/Y <= 0, non-finite or non-positive pixel size, and a buffer size overflow. Kept (required geometry).
3. ArtemisGetMaxBin: old ignored the result and used an uninitialized stack variable (max_x_bin/max_y_bin), so its effective value on failure was undefined; new refused on failure or

Owner (2026-11-23): the Atik Infinity is an AtikCameraSonySci camera in the SDK, the same class as the Atik VS that connects fine with 3.0.0.50 on arm64. This weakens the optional-capability hypothesis (same SDK class, working here) and makes a platform difference (armhf SDK build / 32-bit, Raspberry Pi 3) or an Infinity-specific reply more likely. Not verified on armhf.

Implementer follow-up: 32-bit / armhf scrutiny of the connect and attach path (owner: the Infinity is an AtikCameraSonySci camera like the VS, which connects with 3.0.0.50 on arm64).

COMPILER CHECK of the regenerated indigo_ccd_atik.c (3.0.0.51), -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -funsigned-char (armhf char is unsigned), as ILP32 32-bit ARM (armv7k-apple-watchos, -DINDIGO_LINUX with a malloc.h stub), as ILP32 arm64_32, and native 64-bit (-DINDIGO_MACOS). No armhf Linux cross compiler or sysroot is available on this host, so this approximates armhf (ILP32, 32-bit long/size_t/pointers, unsigned char) and is not an armhf build. All three produce the same 24 warnings; none is specific to 32-bit. Warnings in the connect/attach path:
- 162 atik_option: int id -> unsigned short argument of ArtemisCameraSpecificOptionGetData (ids 1/5/6, harmless).
- 213 overflow guard: int nPixelsY -> size_t divisor (checked > 0 first, harmless).
- 305 buffer_size = 2 * (size_t)nPixelsX * nPixelsY + FITS_HEADER_SIZE: int -> size_t (positive, harmless).
- 306 indigo_alloc_blob_buffer(long size) takes the size_t buffer_size: on 32-bit long is 32-bit signed, so sizes between 2 GB and the SIZE_MAX guard would wrap. Latent only for sensors of about 1 Gpixel; the Infinity (1392 x 1040) needs about 2.9 MB. The old driver had the same long parameter.
Other warnings are outside the connect path (exposure float/double/int conversions, unused callback parameters, the generated retry-handler cast).

MANUAL REVIEW (new vs pre-migration driver, connect and attach):
- struct ARTEMISPROPERTIES: only int, float and char[] fields, no packing pragma; identical layout on armhf and arm64. The new driver zero-initializes it (old did not).
- BOOL is C bool in the SDK header for both driver versions; ArtemisDeviceIsCamera (new in plug) also returns BOOL. The device appeared for the reporter, so plug succeeded.
- Serial and name buffers: new 100 bytes, as the SDK header document

STEP 1 - places where 3.0.0.50 refuses what the pre-migration driver accepted (connect path, call by call):
1. Discovery/open: old plug attached every SDK index even when ArtemisDeviceSerial failed (serial "") and never called ArtemisDeviceIsCamera; old connect used ArtemisConnect(index) directly. New plug skips devices that are not cameras, have no NUL-terminated non-empty serial or no name; atik_open rescans ArtemisDeviceSerial and connects only on a serial match. Not changed: plug and open use the same lookup, the reporter's camera appeared, and the VS run proves the serial lookup works ("65535 65535").
2. ArtemisProperties: both refuse a failed call. New also refuses nPixelsX/Y <= 0, non-finite or non-positive pixel size, and a buffer size overflow. Kept (required geometry).
3. ArtemisGetMaxBin: old ignored the result and used an uninitialized stack variable (max_x_bin/max_y_bin), so its effective value on failure was undefined; new refused on failure or bx/by < 1 or > sensor size. FIXED: 1x1 (no binning) default.
4. ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo(0): old ignored the result (count initialized 0); new refused any result other than OK/NOT_IMPLEMENTED. FIXED: temperature hidden.
5. ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo(1) with sensors > 0: old ignored the result and published 0.0 C as OK; new refused. FIXED: temperature hidden (no invented value).
6. ArtemisCoolingInfo: old ignored the result with flags uninitialized; new refused any result other than OK/NOT_IMPLEMENTED. FIXED: cooler hidden.
7. Cooling flags (flags & 3) == 3 with max <= min: old exposed the cooler and divided by zero for the power; new refused. FIXED: cooler hidden.
8. Cooling flags (flags & 3) == 3 without a temperature sensor: old exposed the cooler; new refused. FIXED: cooler hidden.
9. ArtemisGetWindowHeaterPower failure: old showed X_WINDOW_HEATER in ALERT with an uninitialized value; new refused; out-of-range power 0..255 also refused. FIXED: window heater hidden.
10. Preset readback (option 1) failure or short read: old showed X_PRESETS in ALERT; new refused. FIXED: presets, gain and offset hidden.
11. Preset value > 3: old left the switch unchanged; new refused. FIXED: presets, gain and offset hidden.
12. Preset 0 with gain/offset readback failing or out of range: old published ALERT then overwrote with OK and uninitialized ranges; new refused. FIXED: X_PRESETS shown on CUSTOM in ALERT, CCD_GAIN/CCD_OFFSET hidden (same as X_PRESETS.on_change).
13. Buffer allocation failure: old asserted; new refuses. Kept.
14. Guider device: old ignored ArtemisGuidePort(0) at connect; new refuses the guider connection when it fails. Not changed (out of scope, separate device; the Infinity reportedly has no guide port - not verified).
15. Wheel device: both refuse a failed ArtemisFilterWheelInfo; new also validates count 1..64 and the position. Not changed.

FIX (indigo_ccd_atik.driver, version 50 -> 51, regenerated with the unchanged generator built in the worktree; generated diff = only atik_initialize_ccd and DRIVER_VERSION 0x03000033, .h and _main.c unchanged; regeneration of the unchanged 3.0.0.50 source was byte-identical): only ArtemisProperties, sensor geometry and buffer allocation still refuse the connection; every optional query that fails or answers out of range hides that capability (MaxBin -> 1x1) and logs the SDK result with INDIGO_DRIVER_LOG. No out-of-range value reaches a property; all hidden properties stay hidden for the session, so the 5 s poll never queries a temperature or cooler that is not published.

TESTS (indigo_test/integration/test_ccd_atik_sdk.c; fake SDK gained a per-camera query_error that makes the five optional queries return that code without touching their outputs):
- uncooled_camera_with_failing_capability_queries: uncooled camera, all optional queries ARTEMIS_INVALID_FUNCTION -> connects; CCD_TEMPERATURE, CCD_COOLER, CCD_COOLER_POWER, X_WINDOW_HEATER, X_PRESETS, CCD_GAIN, CCD_OFFSET undefined; CCD_INFO max bin 1/1, CCD_BIN max 1, CCD_MODE = BIN_1x1 only; RAW exposure delivered with verified pixels and SDK bin 1x1; no ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo call after connect over 3 poll periods; disconnect closes; with the queries answering again the same camera connects with all capabilities and max bin 4.
- optional_capability_failures_hide_only_that_capability: 10 sub-cases (TemperatureSensorInfo fails; CoolingInfo fails; cooling max <= min; GetMaxBin fails; max bin 0; GetWindowHeaterPower fails; option GetData fails; short option read; preset 4; preset 0 with gain out of range) -> each connects, hides exactly the expected properties and keeps the others, max bin 1 or 4 as expected, X_PRESETS ALERT/CUSTOM for the gain case, exposure delivered, camera closed after disconnect; final clean connect shows all.
- repeated_connect_during_a_failed_initialization: CONNECT gated inside ArtemisProperties, three more CONNECTION requests (CONNECTED, DISCONNECTED, CONNECTED) while BUSY are ignored; failure gives ALERT, one open and one close, no SDK call after close; next connect, exposure and disconnect work (2 opens, 2 closes).
- Changed expectations: initialization_failures now covers only the hard failures ArtemisConnect and ArtemisProperties (the optional calls moved to the new case with the opposite, pre-migration expectation); malformed_initialization now covers zero sensor width and height (hard failure, camera closed, later connect and exposure work) instead of max bin 0 / cooling max 0 / short option, which moved to the new case.
- Proof of failure without the fix: with the test changes and the 3.0.0.50 driver, uncooled_camera_with_failing_capability_queries failed at its connect (CONNECTION ALERT) and optional_capability_failures_hide_only_that_capability failed at its first sub-case (TemperatureSensorInfo, CONNECTION ALERT); repeated_connect_during_a_failed_initialization passed before and after (it probes the failed-connect path, no defect found). The baseline run of the unchanged suite against 3.0.0.50 was 44/44, with the old initialization_failures/malformed_initialization asserting a refused connection for every item of 3-12 above.

Scenario mapping: uncooled camera connects/hidden capabilities/exposure/reconnect -> uncooled_camera_with_failing_capability_queries; each optional query failure or invalid answer -> optional_capability_failures_hide_only_that_capability; hard failures refuse cleanly and a later connect works -> initialization_failures, malformed_initialization; repeated CONNECTION during a failing connect, balanced open/close, no SDK after close -> repeated_connect_during_a_failed_initialization (+ end_fixture checks of sdk_after_close, sdk_overlap, usb refs, updates after detach). Not covered: image buffer allocation failure (not injectable without a new framework replacement).

RUNS (mac arm64, worktree): baseline make -C indigo_test test-ccd-atik-sdk 44/44 pass on 3.0.0.50; filtered runs of the new/changed cases fail/pass as stated; recorded run python3 tools/run_driver_test.py ccd_atik --no-build: 47/47 OK, record line "2026-11-23 21:56 3.0.0.51 mac arm64 fake SDK 47/47 OK" (README and TEST_SUMMARY.md written by the script). MIGRATION_STATUS.md ccd_atik 44 / 1 -> 47 / 1. flow check (whitespace) passed.
--no-build reason: the plain recorded run failed in the driver build step after the driver compiled cleanly: Makefile.drv runs install_name_tool -id $(BUILD_LIB)/libatikcameras.dylib on the vendor dylib (install name "bin/libatikcameras.dylib", almost no header padding), and the ticket worktree path makes the new id too long ("larger updated load commands do not fit"). This is a macOS build limitation of long checkout paths, unrelated to this change (the primary checkout path is ~60 characters shorter); fixing Makefile.drv was not in scope. The test binary compiles the driver source itself and does not link the archive, so the verdict is unaffected; the partial build products were removed.

EKOS CRASH: unexplained. Checked: the failed-connect path calls atik_close only after a successful atik_open and frees nothing twice (buffer is allocated only on success); CONNECTION requests during a running attempt are ignored by indigo_ignore_connection_change; driver properties are undefined after a failed connect so client changes cannot reach the SDK with a NULL handle (indigo_property_match_changeable requires defined); no timer is started on failure. COMPILER CHECK of the regenerated indigo_ccd_atik.c (3.0.0.51), -fsyntax-only -Wall -Wextra -Wformat=2 -Wconversion -Wsign-conversion -funsigned-char (armhf char is unsigned), as ILP32 32-bit ARM (armv7k-apple-watchos, -DINDIGO_LINUX with a malloc.h stub), as ILP32 arm64_32, and native 64-bit (-DINDIGO_MACOS). No armhf Linux cross compiler or sysroot is available on this host, so this approximates armhf (ILP32, 32-bit long/size_t/pointers, unsigned char) and is not an armhf build. All three produce the same 24 warnings; none is specific to 32-bit. Warnings in the connect/attach path:
- 162 atik_option: int id -> unsigned short argument of ArtemisCameraSpecificOptionGetData (ids 1/5/6, harmless).
- 213 overflow guard: int nPixelsY -> size_t divisor (checked > 0 first, harmless).
- 305 buffer_size = 2 * (size_t)nPixelsX * nPixelsY + FITS_HEADER_SIZE: int -> size_t (positive, harmless).
- 306 indigo_alloc_blob_buffer(long size) takes the size_t buffer_size: on 32-bit long is 32-bit signed, so sizes between 2 GB and the SIZE_MAX guard would wrap. Latent only for sensors of about 1 Gpixel; the Infinity (1392 x 1040) needs about 2.9 MB. The old driver had the same long parameter.
Other warnings are outside the connect path (exposure float/double/int conversions, unused callback parameters, the generated retry-handler cast).

MANUAL REVIEW (new vs pre-migration driver, connect and attach):
- struct ARTEMISPROPERTIES: only int, float and char[] fields, no packing pragma; identical layout on armhf and arm64. The new driver zero-initializes it (old did not).
- BOOL is C bool in the SDK header for both driver versions; ArtemisDeviceIsCamera (new in plug) also returns BOOL. The device appeared for the reporter, so plug succeeded.
- Serial and name buffers: new 100 bytes, as the SDK header documents; the old driver used 64 bytes for the serial (smaller than documented). Comparisons use strcmp/memchr and do not depend on char signedness.
- No pointer-to-int casts in the connect path; ArtemisHandle stays void *.
- Uninitialized values: the old driver used uninitialized flags/level/min/max/set_point, max bin and window-heater power when the SDK did not write them. The new driver initializes all of them, and 3.0.0.51 does not use them after a failed query.
- Timing: the new driver runs the first temperature/cooler poll right after connecting; the old driver waited 5 s. This does not refuse a connection and was not changed.

REMAINING CANDIDATES (none confirmed on an Infinity or on armhf):
1. Optional capability queries answered with an error code by the armhf SDK build. The old driver's "Temporary workaround for SDK_2020_06_23" comment shows that an earlier SDK returned errors from exactly ArtemisTemperatureSensorInfo/ArtemisCoolingInfo, and the VS on arm64 does not exclude a 32-bit-build difference. Fixed in 3.0.0.51.
2. New ArtemisProperties pixel-size validation (non-finite or <= 0 refuses; the old driver accepted any value). Kept as a hard failure because it is part of ArtemisProperties. It would refuse only if the armhf SDK reported a zero or invalid pixel size.
3. Open by serial (atik_open), instead of the old open by index. Proven on arm64 with the VS, not verified on armhf.
4. If the Infinity reports a guide port: ArtemisGuidePort(0) failing now refuses the guider connection; the old driver ignored it. The CCD is not affected.
No 32-bit-specific defect was found. A -vv log from the reporter would decide between 1 to 3. 3.0.0.51 logs each hidden capability with its SDK result code at INFO level.
